title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.

title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design
summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction. An evidence-driven design trajectory for bidirectional in-hand manipulation yielded SAGE Hand (Skill-Aware Generative Embodiment): four fingers, 16 actuated DoF, an integrated guiding palm, compact roots, cylindrical tips, and a collision-cleared opposable thumb. Under a matched training protocol, SAGE Hand reaches 45.6% task success on a hexagonal prism against 37.3% for the LEAP hand, and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder against 51.6%. Dense simulated tactile input more than halves the cylinder drop rate. In a controlled iteration study, the Skill path preserves capture at 164/165 trials while the path without the Skill degrades to 14/165, confirming that the gates act as a regression guard during refinement. Accepted candidates pack with URDF/MJCF, metrics, checkpoints, and a provenance manifest.

title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
summary: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster without cost in quality. A diagnostic using exact facts from maps and annotations yields a 3.6-point margin over its corresponding control, with a 95% confidence interval above zero. title: Report2Alpha-Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents on End-to-End Quantitative Research
summary: We evaluate whether LLM agents can independently carry out a several-hour quantitative research project: read a brokerage research report, make a plan, and over 7 rounds of iteration propose hypotheses, write factor code and improve it from backtest feedback, seeing only 2022-2023 market data. Like Terminal-Bench-Science, the task evaluates overall research ability; unlike it, there is no directly checkable unique answer: the model must repeatedly propose hypotheses on very noisy data, revise its understanding from experiments, disentangle multiple factors and design ablations without overfitting in-sample, much like complex real-world decisions with many interacting factors. After the research, a fixed rule using only 2022-2023 results selects a low-correlated factor pool from all candidates the model produced, and scores it on unseen 2024-2025 data after removing common style returns such as size and momentum; the same rule on round-0 candidates alone gives a report baseline that "implements the report without iterating". We run gpt-6.1-sol (reasoning effort xhigh), gpt-6.1-terra (xhigh), muse-spark-1.3 (xhigh) and deepseek-v4.1-flash (max) once on each of 7 reports. Of the 28 runs, 19 factor pools pass the usability threshold; the average score is 48.4 (0-100 scale), against 25.4 for the report baseline and 35.9 for the models' own picks. From similar report baselines (17.0-31.0), the models separate after iteration to 74.7 (gpt-6.1-sol), 56.6 (gpt-6.1-terra), 35.8 (deepseek-v4.1-flash) and 26.2 (muse-spark-1.3); their candidates look equally good in training and diverge only in testing, with the leaders proposing more diverse ideas per round and ending with more effective factors in the pool. Evaluating research agents thus requires scoring on frozen future data after removing styles, and measuring "what the research produced" separately from "what was finally picked".

title: Learning Inside Types: Epistemic Typestates for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Type disciplines make programs safe by construction: components checked against each other's types compose into programs that cannot go wrong in the ways the types exclude. Types suit reinforcement learning: a type constrains what an agent may choose, not how it chooses, so the guarantee holds for every policy a learner produces. We introduce epistemic typestates, a type discipline for safe multi-agent reinforcement learning. An agent's type is a protocol whose states record its beliefs, the worlds it cannot rule out from its own observations and actions, and permits only actions that are safe in every world of the belief, whatever the others do within their public types. Agents learn inside their types, which are built and checked one agent at a time and run without communication. We prove type soundness and team safety, give a synthesis that is sound and complete, build types from guards when worlds are infinite, and show that shields are a special case. All proofs are mechanised in Rocq. On nine benchmarks, no typed learner causes a safety violation, and task performance does not differ significantly from that of two recent multi-agent shielding methods. Where a contract-based method fails at five and ten agents, types for ten agents are built in under a second. In the two continuous benchmarks, Lagrangian learners cause thousands of violations in every training run.

title: Segment Everything, Materialize Nothing: Exact Streaming Inference for Many-Class 3D Segmentation
summary: Whole-body segmentation tools such as TotalSegmentator and MOOSE split more than 100 classes across five or six networks. The reason is memory. Standard 3D inference, as implemented in nnU-Net and MONAI, holds a logit for every class and voxel, on the working grid and again on the scanner's grid. For a median whole-body CT at 125 classes, that is 76 GB. We show that this memory wall lies in what inference materializes, not in the task, and remove it without approximation. Every step after the network is local along one axis, so its outputs can be streamed through a ring one patch thick. The classification head commutes with blending and resampling, so the ring carries the network's features instead of the class logits. Memory thus no longer grows with classes times volume, and the label map on the scanner's grid stays exact. This holds for any model with a pointwise affine head, without retraining. Many-class models, previously impractical, become deployable. One model trained on all classes matches or slightly exceeds the toolkits' five or six specialists in segmentation quality and runs 5.8-15x faster end to end, with 3.2-7.6x less RAM and under 8 GB of VRAM. We provide the method as a drop-in for nnU-Net, TotalSegmentator and MOOSE. The code is part of nnU-Net (https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet), and unified models for both toolkits will be released.

title: Criterion and Construction Framework for Impure Quantum $(r,δ)$-LRCs from Optimal $(r,δ)$-LRCs
summary: This paper aims to uncover new phenomena and provide new tools for quantum \((r,δ)\)-LRCs derived from optimal \((r,δ)\)-LRCs. title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
summary: Public benchmarks guide model selection, post-training rewards and claims of progress in artificial intelligence, yet leaderboards report aggregate scores without verifying whether each task's prompt, environment and grader agree on what counts as success. How often that agreement fails in contemporary evaluations, and in which direction confirmed defects move scores, has remained unmeasured across grading designs. Here we synthesize task-level quality reviews of 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations spanning closed-form question answering, document rubrics and agentic execution to assess whether prompts, environments and graders align. Task validity stratifies sharply by grading architecture. Closed-form benchmarks revised after public error reporting reach 92.5% verified validity, compared with 29.3% across six multi-step suites that nevertheless already supply 161 verified complex tasks. Rubric suites fail through mismatches between prompts and reference checklists, whereas execution harnesses add incomplete state assertions, shared-channel leaks and grading-time collisions. Across confirmed defects, 71.7% withhold credit from compliant solutions while 28.3% permit shortcut passes, indicating that raw leaderboard ceilings understate frontier capability on many practical tasks. Grading committed patches inside a fresh container cuts confirmed runtime bypasses from 14.7% in shared containers to 2.7% (a 5.5x drop, and 0% in read-only or static suites), showing how targeted maintenance restores existing benchmarks at low cost. As the initial milestone of the long-term Benchmarks' Last Exam initiative, this synthesis launches sustained expansion across wider benchmark coverage and deeper evaluation-quality dimensions so that pursuing leaderboard gains directly advances genuine model capability.
